prompt:
Precise-object-edit / geometry correction for ONE 40px medieval iron-mine menu icon.
INPUT1 is the user's REAL PICKAXE PHOTOGRAPH: authoritative reference for the physical geometry of head, oval eye and wooden handle. INPUT2 is the current icon: reference for muted colour/material, ore and tight framing ONLY. Its tool geometry is WRONG, do not preserve that geometry.
Create the mine icon with a pickaxe constructed EXACTLY like the real tool in input1. The long main axis connecting the steel head's two working ends is PERPENDICULAR (90 DEGREES) to the straight wooden shaft at the central mounting eye. This MUST be visibly a T-shaped junction, NOT nearly parallel or an acute 30 degree junction as in input2.
For a readable icon, use a nearly front-on view of the tool's plane: head runs from approximately upper-left (15%,18%) to mid-right (85%,48%), shaft runs from the central eye near (50%,33%) down-left toward (22%,90%), forming an obvious RIGHT ANGLE in the image. The head's span vector is (70,30); the shaft direction is (-30,70), their dot product is zero. This is a composition guide, not text to draw. The shaft must fit through the CENTRAL oval eye in a single straight line with no kink, no side-mounted connection, no distorted elbow. Both metal ends project from the eye crosswise to the haft, as in the real photograph. Use a narrow pick point and a modest flat narrow chisel end like the photo; no huge axe blade and no double fantasy scythe.
Keep two angular dark iron ore fragments at lower RIGHT of frame, supporting this tool without obscuring central eye. Tool head and mounting eye dominate the tightly cropped square, handle can exit bottom-left. Realistic grey weathered iron, desaturated grey-brown ashwood, charcoal ore with restrained rusty traces, cold soft upper-left light. Same restrained cinematic material treatment as input2, but geometrically faithful to input1. No bright orange wood, no decoration, no abstract symbol, no scene. True transparent RGBA background. No text, no outline frame. High resolution square source.
